entries.name: jq
entries.description: Turn JSON exports and API responses into filtered records, aggregates, or input for another command.
entries.notes: Registry key: `jq` (aqua backend available). Declare `jq = "1.8"` under `[tools]` to share a version across local tasks and CI. Useful for repeatable data-processing tasks without a custom application.

entries.name: yq
entries.description: Query and transform YAML configuration, including conversion between structured data formats.
entries.notes: Registry key: `yq`; choose the Mike Farah implementation, such as `aqua:mikefarah/yq`. Pin it in a project so configuration-editing tasks use the same CLI; unrelated tools also use the name yq.

entries.name: Pandoc
entries.description: Convert documents between formats and build repeatable publishing workflows from source files.
entries.notes: Registry key: `pandoc` (GitHub backend available). Pair a project version with mise tasks for document exports. Some output formats require additional software; PDF output may need a separate PDF engine.

entries.name: Rclone
entries.description: Copy, inspect, and synchronize files across local storage and cloud providers.
entries.notes: Registry key: `rclone` (aqua backend available). Useful in named transfer or backup tasks. Remotes need separate configuration and credentials; inspect a dry run before adopting operations that can delete destination files.

entries.name: Document inventory
entries.description: Create a CSV of relative file paths and byte sizes, with input and output locations set by the project environment.
entries.notes: Requires Python 3.11+ as `python3` and an existing `documents/` directory. Creates or replaces `build/inventory.csv`; excludes directories and symbolic links. For a quick trial, create `documents/hello.txt` containing `hello` followed by a newline: its row is `hello.txt,6`. Paths are relative to documents/.

entries.name: CSV category totals
entries.description: Summarize a CSV by category into a JSON report, with a preparation task creating the output directory.
entries.notes: Requires a POSIX shell and Python 3.11+ as `python3` and `input.csv` with `category,amount` headers and integer amounts. Creates or replaces `build/totals.json`. Rows `books,12`, `food,8`, and `books,3` produce totals books=15 and food=8. Task dependencies keep output preparation ahead of report generation.

entries.name: Portable notes archive
entries.description: Package a notes directory into a gzip-compressed tar archive using a named task.
entries.notes: Requires Python 3.11+ as `python3` and an existing `notes/` directory. Creates or replaces `build/notes.tar.gz`; includes the notes directory and its contents. For a trial, add notes/hello.txt and inspect the resulting archive with `python3 -m tarfile -l build/notes.tar.gz`. Archive creation is not a complete backup strategy.

entries.name: mise-action
entries.description: Install project tools in GitHub Actions so CI can use the same mise configuration as contributors.
entries.notes: Official action with installation and caching options. Follow upstream examples for action versions and runner requirements; declare project tools in mise configuration rather than duplicating version choices in workflow steps.

entries.name: mise-vscode
entries.description: Discover and run project tasks, manage tools, and work with the mise environment from VS Code.
entries.notes: Community extension. Inspect its environment and supported language-extension settings; automatic configuration of other extensions is optional. Remote development needs mise on the machine running the extension.

entries.name: intellij-mise
entries.description: Connect mise-managed SDKs and tasks to JetBrains IDEs.
entries.notes: Community plugin for the IntelliJ platform. Review upstream IDE compatibility and SDK support; useful when an IDE and an interactive terminal select different runtimes.

entries.name: mise development workflow
entries.description: Study how mise itself combines a toolchain, separate task files, documentation generation, and build/test orchestration.
entries.notes: Configuration case study. Start with `[task_config].includes`, then read [tasks.toml](https://github.com/jdx/mise/blob/main/tasks.toml) for the `ci` dependency graph and `render:*` tasks. Commands depend on the mise source tree and development tools; use individual patterns rather than running the configuration in an unrelated project.

entries.name: mise-action maintenance workflow
entries.description: See a JavaScript GitHub Action use mise for linting, testing, versioning, and release tasks.
entries.notes: Configuration case study. Inspect the concise `tasks.*` declarations and `[tools]`, then follow referenced scripts in the repository. Its pre-commit task stages generated files with git add; review side effects before adapting it. This is the action project development setup, separate from installing the action in your own CI.

entries.name: Python environments and uv scripts
entries.description: Choose between a requirements-based virtualenv, a uv project, and scripts with inline dependencies.
entries.notes: Official walkthrough with complete configurations and expected project files. Particularly useful for deciding which component owns Python versions, virtualenv creation, and dependency installation.

entries.name: Terraform and OpenTofu workflows
entries.description: Wrap infrastructure initialization, validation, planning, and application in project tasks.
entries.notes: Official walkthrough showing subdirectory commands and dependency ordering. Initialization can download providers and change a lockfile; apply and destroy change infrastructure and require separate care and credentials.
